messages:
Maya: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands runtime segment 5: is there an official playbook for when to prioritize kernel work vs batching/caching?
Diego: Not yet a single doc, but we're drafting one. Kernels = tail latency/spec hardware wins; batching/caching = $/token and per-tenant boosts.
Maya: Can we include concrete examples so PMs have numbers?
Sana: Yes. Examples we'll include: attention fusion gave ~10-15% P95 improvement on long-seq; auto-batcher experiment showed ~18% cost drop for chat workloads.
Corey: Rollout notes: kernel changes require model-specific perf tests and slower canaries; batching rules can be toggled per-tenant.
Maya: Ops question 5: will kernel upgrades require reboots for Dedicated or Private?
Diego: Most dedicated pools support live kernel swap. Older on-prem images might need rolling restarts; we'll list affected images.
Deploy Bot: deploy-bot started canary kernel-fusion-v5 on pool:dedicated-eu at 1915550100 10% traffic.
Sana: We'll add an ops checklist in the playbook: quick logs to check, grep patterns, and rollback knobs (per-pool kernel select, disable auto-batcher, pin model+kernel).
Maya: Leadership asked for rough timeline buckets (fast/typical/slow) 5: can we add ranges?
Corey: Proposal: fast = 1-2w (config + batching rules), typical = 4-8w (auto-batch tuning + infra), slow = 2-4+ months (kernel impl + validation).
Maya: Great. Action items: Diego draft skeleton by Wed, Sana add ops checks, Corey add timeline examples. I'll collate PM-facing summary once draft's up.
Diego: Will post draft to eng-runtime and ping PMs.
Maya: Thanks everyone 44d closing once draft is live.
